historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: GAAP revenue 3yr CAGR 2.2% plus management's high-single-digit earnings-growth framework (ex legacy VA) haircut for run-off; equity CAGRs are broken by LDTI and AOCI
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-13.6%) is an accounting artefact: LDTI restated FY2021 equity from ~$63.7bn to ~$30bn and AOCI swings billions with rates. GAAP EPS 3yr/5yr CAGRs are undefined (FY2022 EPS -4.49, FY2020 -1.00); FY2023 -> FY2025 GAAP EPS went 6.76 -> 10.05. No owner-FCF series exists for an insurer (OCF less capex is not free cash), so FCF CAGRs are null.
historical_growth.notes: GAAP revenue (CSV) is volatile from PRT single premiums and realized gains: 57,033 (FY2020), 71,247 (FY2021), 56,881 (FY2022), 53,979 (FY2023), 70,405 (FY2024), 60,774 (FY2025). Annual CAGRs are unchanged from the prior build (no new fiscal year). RESTATED adjusted revenue FY2025 55,837; 9M-2026 41,733 vs 41,788. RESTATED after-tax AOI FY2025 4,894 (9M 3,764 + Q4 1,130); 9M-2026 3,845 (+2%; Q1 1,204 / Q2 1,320 / Q3 1,321 vs Q3-2025 1,444); AOI EPS 9M-2026 $10.91 vs $10.49. Adjusted book value per share $102.39 vs $99.25 a year earlier.

scenario_narratives.base: A US-centred retirement, life and asset-management franchise with a Japan business under regulatory orders and an emerging-markets exit that is now largely contracted. The Japan drag is bigger and longer than the October build assumed (~$600M in 2026, ~$700M in 2027, a tail into 2028) because the FSA turned a voluntary pause into a suspension order and pulled in Gibraltar. Against that, Brazil and Mexico were sold for $4.0bn -- more than the whole programme was pitched to release -- and roughly half the $750M cost programme sticks. Conversion of AOI into distributable cash edges up from 60% to 64%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Japan returns to market in February 2027 with improvement plans accepted and the damage proves temporary; the full cost programme drops through; PGIM and retail annuities keep growing; a simpler, less capital-hungry group converts 70% of earnings to cash and re-rates toward MET.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FSA keeps Prudential of Japan out of the market well into 2027, the Life Planner force and in-force book shrink, and Japan settles at permanently lower earnings. Lower rates and a credit cycle compress spreads and PGIM flows; savings are absorbed. Earnings stall below today's level and conversion stays under what is being paid out.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value PRU on the cash its holding company can actually return to shareholders (FCFE), discounted at a 10% cost of equity with debt held inside the flows. Earnings are built from adjusted operating income on the restated (ex-emerging-markets) basis, but the cash conversion is set to what PRU has actually distributed (~60% of restated AOI), so the AOI-to-GAAP gap is priced in rather than ignored. The businesses being sold are valued at their contracted net sale price in the equity bridge. The Japan regulatory orders are modelled from management's own disclosed impact figures, extended in base and stressed in bear. Adjusted book ($102.39) and operating ROE (~14.5%) are a cross-check, not the driver.
key_risks_to_valuation: Japan: sales resumption after 31 January 2027 depends on the FSA accepting business improvement plans; management says the drag grows if the suspension extends, and flags reputational spillover; base assumes Japan earnings power is eventually restored
Brazil/Mexico sale ($3.1bn net, ~$8/share in the bridge) has not closed: regulatory approvals in two countries, closing adjustments, BRL/MXN moves before H2-2027

Cash conversion: organic holdco cash generation ran ~50% of AOI in 9M-2026 against ~58% distributed, the gap met with net debt issuance; if 60% is not organically sustainable the base is ~$10/share too high
Interest rates and spreads: Retirement and Japan spread income are rate-sensitive; AOCI fell $2.7bn in Q3-2026; legacy VA/GUL blocks carry equity-market and policyholder-behaviour risk
Earnings quality: GAAP NI runs well below AOI once divested-business earnings are stripped out; net credit-related losses rose to $184M pre-tax in Q3-2026
Yen: Japan earnings and capital translate at the prevailing JPY/USD rate
PGIM: affiliated outflows ($6.5bn in 9M-2026) and the shift away from active equity pressure fees; Retirement net withdrawals of $1.4bn in 9M-2026

unchanged_assumptions.cost_of_equity: 10.0% in all scenarios -- unchanged. Would move on a sustained shift in the 10-year UST of more than ~75bp, or down toward MET's 9.5% once Japan is trading normally for a year under accepted improvement plans.
unchanged_assumptions.terminal: Terminal growth 2.5/3.0/2.0% and FCFE multiple caps 13x/14x/11x (base/bull/bear) -- unchanged.
unchanged_assumptions.weights: 25/50/25 -- unchanged. The regulator's response and the Gibraltar spillover that justified the 25% bear are now known and inside base, which argues for a lighter bear; against that the return to market now needs FSA sign-off on improvement plans rather than a date PRU chose. The two roughly offset. Would move bear toward 15-20% on sales actually resuming in February 2027 and the Brazil/Mexico sale closing.
unchanged_assumptions.growth_fy2028_onward: Revenue growth from FY2028 (base 4.0 -> 2.5%, bull 5.0 -> 3.0%, bear 2.0-2.5 -> 2.0%) -- unchanged. Only FY2026 (marked to 9M actuals) and FY2027 (Japan premiums, -0.5pt in each scenario) moved. Would move on two or more quarters of Retirement net flows staying negative (9M-2026 net withdrawals $1.4bn) or a step change in pension-risk-transfer volumes.
unchanged_assumptions.steady_state_margin: Base 12.2% and bull 13.15% from FY2029-30 are the prior 12.5% / 13.5% less the ~0.33pt the restatement removed (FY2025 margin 11.95% old basis -> 11.62% restated) -- unchanged like-for-like. BEAR is the one later-year path that WAS re-judged: 11.0% against a like-for-like 11.2%, because a regulator-imposed order that reached Gibraltar makes a lasting loss of Japan earnings a credible downside rather than a tail. Would move on evidence of how much of the $750M drops through (first disclosure expected with FY2026 results) or a permanent impairment of Japan earnings power.
unchanged_assumptions.sbc_and_later_tax: SBC 0.46% of revenue (same $257M) and the 21.5% AOI tax rate from FY2027 -- unchanged; only FY2026 tax is marked to the 20.0% 9M actual.
unchanged_assumptions.model_and_net_debt: FCFE at cost of equity, net debt zero, parent liquid assets not added, flat share count -- unchanged.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 total ADJUSTED revenues on the RESTATED basis (emerging-market businesses, incl. Brazil and Mexico, moved to Divested and Run-off from Q3-2026 and applied retrospectively): 9M-2025 41,788 + Q4-2025 14,049 (Q3-2026 Quarterly Financial Supplement, 8-K 2026-11-03 Ex 99.2). The prior build used 57,677 on the old basis; the 1,840 difference is the exited businesses. 9M-2026 41,733 (Q1 14,685 / Q2 13,555 / Q3 13,493). Premiums are lumpy (pension-risk-transfer single premiums; Q3-2025 was 15,742), so revenue-based margins carry quarter noise.
inputs.share_count_basis: 347.7M end-of-period DILUTED common shares at 30 September 2026 (Q3-2026 earnings release, adjusted book value table). Cross-check: 343M basic outstanding at 30 October 2026 (10-Q cover) plus ~3-4M dilutive awards. Held FLAT: SBC is charged in the flows, and the $1.0bn/yr repurchase programme ($746M done in 9M-2026) is a use of the FCFE being capitalised, not extra growth.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO. Total debt $20,730M at 30 September 2026 = capital debt $14,341M + operating debt $5,986M + limited/non-recourse ~$403M (QFS debt table). Interest on capital debt sits inside Corporate & Other adjusted operating income (interest expense on debt $689M in 9M-2026; holdco net interest paid $896M), and operating debt is matched by the assets it funds, so the AOI-based flow is already post-financing; deducting debt again would count it twice. Consolidated cash ($18,692M at 30 September 2026) is general-account and policyholder liquidity, not surplus. Parent highly liquid assets of $4,010M (ex intercompany liquidity account) are treated as the required holdco buffer and NOT added.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 capital returned to common shareholders: dividends $1,932M + repurchases $1,000M (QFS). Used as the observed FCFE proxy = 60% of FY2025 after-tax AOI on the restated basis ($4,894M; it was 57% of the old-basis $5,161M). 9M-2026: capital returned $2,230M = 58% of after-tax AOI $3,845M, while ORGANIC holdco cash generation (business capital activity $2,453M less net interest $896M, plus tax, other corporate, employee share issuance and affiliated operating flows) was ~$1.94bn = ~50%, the gap funded by $483M of net debt issuance. Subsidiary dividends are lumpy and 9M-2025 ran lower still, so the distribution-based 60% is kept as the base anchor, but this is the reason bear holds conversion at 57%. An insurer's OCF-less-capex is not free cash, so the owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income is deliberately not satisfied.
inputs.sbc_source: PRU_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2025 $257M (SEC XBRL, cash-flow add-back); FY2024 $314M, FY2023 $254M. Award-settlement withholding is not separately disclosed and is immaterial against the $1bn buyback; charged at 0.46% of restated adjusted revenue (257 / 55,837).
inputs.buyback_note: Repurchases $1,000M in each of FY2023 (1,012), FY2024 and FY2025; $746M in 9M-2026 ($250M a quarter; 2026 authorisation $1.0bn). End-of-period diluted count 353.9M (Sep-25) -> 347.7M (Sep-26), -1.8%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 10.0% (USD flows): 10-year UST ~4.3% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.15, rounded up. Half a point above the 9.5% used for MET because PRU carries the same rate/credit/equity sensitivity plus a live governance failure in its largest international unit (Prudential of Japan), a run-off legacy variable-annuity and GUL block, a five-year divestiture programme and a persistent gap between GAAP net income and AOI. It is a cost of equity, not a WACC, because the flows are post-interest FCFE. Same rate in all three scenarios; scenario risk sits in the driver paths and weights, not a stacked discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: operating leases are immaterial for an insurer and their cost is already inside the AOI expense base.
inputs.nci_treatment: None in the flows or bridge: adjusted operating income EXCLUDES earnings attributable to noncontrolling and redeemable noncontrolling interests, so AOI is already attributable to PFI. The NCI share of 9M-2026 net income was $77M.
inputs.preferred_treatment: No preferred stock outstanding. The 4.125%/5.625%/5.950% junior subordinated notes (PFH/PRS/PRH) are debt; their interest is inside AOI.
inputs.notes: MODEL (unchanged from 2026-10-02): FCFE at cost of equity on a diversified life insurer / asset manager, run through the component engine with net debt at zero -- the MET / GL / IAG.AX cost-of-equity-stream precedent. The dcf-methods routing default for an insurer is BVPS-compounding x exit P/B; overridden because (1) GAAP book is not a usable compounding base: LDTI restated equity from $63.7bn (FY2019) / $68.2bn (FY2020) to ~$30bn (FY2021 restated), and AOCI (-$6.9bn at 30 September 2026, from -$4.1bn at June) moves billions with rates; (2) PRU does not compound book -- it distributes ~60% of AOI (~$2.9-3.0bn/yr) and adjusted book per share grew 3.2% in the year to September 2026 ($99.25 -> $102.39); the value driver is the cash the holding company can distribute. WHAT CHANGED IN THIS UPDATE: (a) BASIS -- from Q3-2026 PRU reports AOI excluding the emerging-market businesses it is exiting (retrospectively applied), so the revenue base, margins and conversion are all re-expressed on the restated basis and the exited units are valued through the equity bridge at their agreed sale price instead of inside the flows; (b) JAPAN -- the FSA's 9 October 2026 business suspension order replaces the assumption that sales resume on 5 November 2026; (c) anchors -- price, 30 September 2026 share count, debt and book value. The cost of equity, terminal growth, terminal multiples, scenario weights, hurdle rate, growth from FY2028 and the steady-state margin level (on a like-for-like basis) are deliberately UNCHANGED; see unchanged_assumptions. EARNINGS ANCHOR: adjusted operating income, not GAAP net income. AOI strips out mark-to-market noise (market-risk-benefit changes, hedge marks, experience-rated pass-throughs) but also excludes real costs -- net credit-related losses ($184M pre-tax in Q3-2026, up from ~$75M a quarter) and some realized losses. 9M-2026 GAAP NI was $2,970M against after-tax AOI $3,845M, and that NI INCLUDES $692M pre-tax of Divested and Run-off earnings that AOI excludes, so the like-for-like gap is wider. The gap is handled by calibrating the FCFE conversion to cash actually returned (~60% of restated AOI), not to AOI itself. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total adjusted revenues; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax AOI BEFORE stock compensation as % of adjusted revenue (FY2025 restated: (6,233 + 257) / 55,837 = 11.62%; old basis 11.95%); sbc_pct_path 0.46%; da_pct_path 0; cash_tax_rate_path = AOI effective tax (FY2025 restated 1,339/6,233 = 21.5%; 9M-2026 962/4,807 = 20.0%, used for FY2026 only), so (margin - SBC) x (1 - tax) = after-tax AOI; capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED in the insurance subsidiaries (new-business strain, RBC/ESR growth, capital contributions, holdco costs, the economic part of GAAP-only credit losses), set so FCFE = the scenario's conversion of after-tax AOI. BVPS CROSS-CHECK: adjusted book value $102.39/share, GAAP BV $84.88, GAAP ex-AOCI $104.59 (30 September 2026; adjusted book $35,602M). The price is ~1.19x adjusted book against a 14.5% operating ROE (9M-2026) but ~10-11% on GAAP earnings; at a 10% cost of equity and 3% growth that brackets a justified P/B of ~1.1x (GAAP ROE) to ~1.65x (operating ROE). Capital: PICA RBC 415% at 31 Dec 2025; total capital $50.7bn (equity ex-AOCI $36.4bn, junior subordinated $7.6bn, other capital debt $6.7bn); management does not expect a material capital, ESR or cash-flow impact from the Japan orders.
inputs.japan_suspension_treatment: FACTS MOVED. The voluntary suspension did NOT lapse on 5 November 2026: on 9 October 2026 Japan's FSA issued a business suspension ORDER barring Prudential of Japan from soliciting new business through 31 January 2027, a PARTIAL suspension order on Gibraltar Life's Life Consultant channel (13 October 2026 - 31 January 2027; independent agency channel unaffected), and business improvement orders to Prudential of Japan, Gibraltar and Prudential Holdings of Japan (plans due end-November 2026, regular progress reports). Management's estimates (Q3-2026 10-Q, Company Overview): Prudential of Japan cut pre-tax AOI by $375M in 9M-2026, ~$500M for FY2026 and $500-550M for FY2027; Gibraltar ~$100M in 2026 and ~$175M in 2027; more if the suspension runs past January 2027; possible reputational spillover to other Japan businesses; no material capital, ESR or cash-flow impact expected. Japan Businesses AOI was $559M in Q3-2026 vs $750M a year earlier, sales -36% constant-dollar. So the combined drag is ~$600M in 2026 and ~$700M in 2027, against the ~$550M / ~$425M the 2 October base assumed -- the 2027 figure is now above what the prior BEAR assumed (~$645M), and the Gibraltar spillover the prior bear feared is in management's own base. Customer reimbursement itself is small (approved claims ~JPY 4bn, ~$27M). TREATMENT: base takes the guided midpoints, resumption on 1 February 2027 and a residual ~$200M drag in FY2028 that the prior build did not have (the 2027 guide rising rather than falling says the ramp is slow); bull takes the low end and a clean 2028; bear extends the suspension several months into 2027 (~$1.0bn drag) and leaves a permanently smaller Japan franchise.
inputs.strategy_overhaul_treatment: FACTS MOVED. The emerging-markets exit has gone from plan to signed contracts in three months: Prudential of Brazil and Prudential of Mexico sold to CNP Assurances for $4.025bn cash (announced 20 October 2026) = ~$3.1bn after transaction costs and taxes (10-Q), expected to close in the second half of 2027 subject to regulatory approvals; Indonesia JV (49%) and ICEA Lion (Kenya, 24%) sales CLOSED in October 2026; agreements signed in September 2026 to sell the 33% stake in Alexander Forbes (South Africa); PGIM India sale to TVS Venu pending. The 40% AFP Habitat (Chile) interest is retained and moved into the Retirement segment. Brazil/Mexico alone deliver the 'well north of $3bn' capital release originally pitched for the whole five-year programme. ACCOUNTING: from Q3-2026 the exited businesses are in Divested and Run-off (outside AOI), retrospectively. That removed ~$400M of FY2025 pre-tax AOI (6,637 -> 6,233), ~$267M after tax (5,161 -> 4,894) and $1,840M of adjusted revenue; 'Other' Divested and Run-off income was $649M pre-tax in 9M-2026. A $80M net tax charge was booked in Q3-2026 on the change in the permanent-reinvestment assertion. TREATMENT: (a) the 2 October build kept the exited businesses' earnings in the flows and added no proceeds ('value-neutral'). Now that reported AOI excludes them and a price is contracted, the flows are on the restated basis and the Brazil/Mexico proceeds enter equity_bridge at $2,800M = $3.1bn net discounted ~one year at the 10% cost of equity. Not counted, as an offsetting conservatism: the earnings these businesses generate until closing, and the undisclosed proceeds of the Indonesia, Kenya, Alexander Forbes and PGIM India sales. The bridge is the same in all three scenarios (a signed cash price). (b) COST SAVES ($750M annual by year-end 2028, reaffirmed in the Q3 10-Q) enter the margin path as before: base keeps roughly half after reinvestment, legacy-VA run-off, stranded overhead and PGIM fee pressure; bull ~all. (c) FCF CONVERSION on the restated AOI base: 60% now (was 57% on the old basis -- the same dollars over a smaller AOI), rising to 64% by FY2030 in base (was 63%), 70% in bull (unchanged level), 57% flat in bear (was 55%). Holding base at 64% rather than marking it up the full ~3.5pt the restatement implies is deliberate: part of the cash PRU distributed came from the units being sold.

bear.narrative: The FSA does not release Prudential of Japan on 31 January 2027: the suspension runs several more months, surrenders stay elevated, Life Planner attrition shrinks the sales force and Gibraltar's Life Consultant channel is slow to recover -- 2027 Japan drag ~$1.0bn rather than ~$700M, and a permanently smaller Japan franchise. Rates fall and spreads compress in Retirement; a credit cycle hits PGIM private credit; cost saves are absorbed by remediation and stranded emerging-market overhead. Margin 10.9% in FY2027-28 and 11.0% steady state (FY2025 restated: 11.62%) -- 0.2pt below the like-for-like level the October bear used, i.e. ~$120M a year of Japan earnings that never come back. Conversion stays at 57%, three points under what is being distributed. Terminal min(Gordon 10%/2%, 11x).

base.narrative: RESTATED BASIS (emerging-market units now outside AOI). FY2026: adjusted revenue flat on FY2025's 55,837 (9M 41,733 vs 41,788; H1 +8%, Q3 -14% against the Q3-2025 pension-risk-transfer spike); pre-tax AOI ~$6.16bn = 9M actual 4,807 + Q4 ~1,355, the Q4 carrying ~$125M of Prudential of Japan drag, the new ~$100M Gibraltar Life hit and a seasonally heavy Corporate & Other loss; AOI tax 20.0% (9M actual) -> after-tax ~$4.9bn, ~$14.1 per diluted share. FY2027: the FSA order moves the guided Japan drag UP to ~$700M ($500-550M Prudential of Japan + ~$175M Gibraltar) from ~$600M in 2026, so the margin slips to 11.4% even as cost saves begin. FY2028: a residual ~$200M Japan drag (sales ramp, business-improvement-plan costs) holds the margin at 11.8%; FY2029 12.1%; steady state 12.2% from FY2030 (= the prior 12.5% less the 0.33pt the restatement removed). Conversion of after-tax AOI to distributable cash 60% in FY2026 (capital returned ~$2.97bn / ~$4.9bn) rising to 64% by FY2030. Brazil/Mexico net proceeds sit in the equity bridge, not the flows. Terminal min(Gordon 10%/2.5%, 13x FCFE).

bull.narrative: Japan sales resume 1 February 2027 with the FSA accepting the improvement plans, the 2027 drag lands at the low end (~$675M) and is gone by 2028; the full $750M of savings reaches the bottom line by 2028-29; PGIM keeps taking third-party flows ($9.0bn in Q3-2026, best in ten quarters) and record RILA sales sustain 4-5% revenue growth. Margin to 13.15% on the restated basis (after-tax AOI ~10% of revenue). With the capital-hungry emerging-market units gone and legacy VA running off, conversion rises from 61% to 70% by FY2030. Terminal min(Gordon 10%/3%, 14x).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the Japan suspension has already been extended once, the regulator's response is open, the 10-Q itself flags possible spillover to Gibraltar Life, and a leveraged spread balance sheet has asymmetric downside in a rate-and-credit downturn. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to happen together -- on-time Japan resumption with a fast ramp, the full $750M of saves, EM sales at premium prices, and a 70% conversion rate PRU has not delivered. Same 25/50/25 as MET, the closest comparable.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
